comments.author: Alexander Terp
comments.body:
Fixed. deps/rad.pin now names rad 0.12.0, whose shell interpolation quotes every value it substitutes - verified against the released binary:

    v = "Developer ID Application: Alexander Terp (CV4835A2BN)"
    $`echo -s {v}`
    -> echo -s 'Developer ID Application: Alexander Terp (CV4835A2BN)'

That also settles the follow-up this card asked for. The sweep does not have to check each interpolation in ./dev one by one, because the quoting is systematic rather than per-site: no value a user can put a space or a bracket in reaches bash unquoted any more.

release.yml then cut v0.1.1 end to end - built, signed with the Developer ID, notarized, stapled, and published - in 4m48s with no local involvement. spctl on the published artifact reports accepted, source=Notarized Developer ID.

creator: Alexander Terp
description:
`release.yml` gets as far as signing and dies there. All seven secrets are set and correct - the Developer ID certificate imports fine - so this is `./dev`, not credentials.

The identity is `Developer ID Application: Alexander Terp (CV4835A2BN)`, and the parentheses are the problem. `sign_developer_id` interpolates it into a shell command:

```
$`codesign -f -s {identity} --options runtime --timestamp {path}`
```

Under CI's rad it arrives unquoted, so bash reads `(CV4835A2BN)` as a subshell:

```
/bin/bash: -c: line 0: syntax error near unexpected token `('
```

**It works locally and fails in CI, which is the part worth writing down.** The same command from the same file on this laptop emits `codesign -f -s 'Developer ID Application: Alexander Terp (CV4835A2BN)' ...` - quoted, correct, and the artifact v0.1.0 ships was signed and notarized that way. Both rads report `v0.11.0` and `deps/rad.pin` names 0.11.0, so the version strings agree while the behaviour does not; the laptop is evidently running a build ahead of the released one. Per amterp, the quoting fix is in rad 0.12, which is not released yet.

So the fix is a pin bump once 0.12 is out, then re-run the workflow. Worth checking at the same time whether any other interpolation in `./dev` carries a value a user could put a space or a bracket in - the identity is the one that bit, but it is not obviously the only candidate, and this is a failure that a laptop cannot reproduce.

Not blocking anything shipped: v0.1.0 is public, installable through the tap, and its artifact was built and notarized locally. What is missing is the ability to cut the *next* release from a tag, which is what `release.yml` exists for.
title: 🔏 The release workflow cannot sign, and only in CI
